answer: For a poll on a meadow beacon shaped like a vertex, officials randomly audit one ID per ten-ballot batch against the roll. If it mismatches, they audit every ID in that batch and reject mismatches; otherwise all ten count. Incomplete batches are rejected. If one invalid ID is present, it has a 10% chance of triggering the full audit, risking other invalid ballots. Borrowed IDs can pass, and errors can reject genuine voters.
